item.title: Drone Signals
item.description:
There are ….

DGI:

  1. Lightbridge Used primarily for mid/pro/legacy models. Examples of models that use this technology are: DJI Inspire 2 (Lightbrindge 2), DJI Matrice 100, DJI Matrice 600 (Lightbridge 2).

  2. Wi-Fi or Enhanced Wi-Fi Used in lighter, entry level and early models of DGI drones. Examples of models that use this technology are: DGI Spark, DJI Mavic Mini, DJI Mini SE and DJI Air (original).

  3. Ocusync This is the modern go-to link for DGI drones. Examples of models that use this technology are: DJI Mini 2 (Ocusync 2.0), DJI Mini 3 Pro (Ocusync 3.0), DJI Mavic Pro (Ocusync 1.0), DJI Mavic 2 Pro (Ocusync 2.0), DJI Air 2S (Ocusync 3.0), DJI Mavic 3 (Ocusync 3+).

item.title: Fast Correlation
item.description:
There are two methods for computing the correlation of complex-valued signals. The first one is a time-domain method, and for a stationary process can be computed using the following formula

$$ r(k) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{N} \sum^{N-k-1}_{n=0} x(n+k)h^{\ast}(n) & \text{if } 0 \leq k \leq N-1 \\ r^{\ast}(-k) & \text{if } -(N-1) \leq k \lt 0 \\ 0 & \text{if } elsewhere \end{cases} $$

where N is the input data record length, x(n) is the input data and h(n) is the kernel, or reference data. The computational time to compute a correlation using this method is directly proportional to the number of samples in the kernel. Therefore, the longer the kernel data record the more time it takes to compute a correlation.
